set.body:
A tolerance constant must declare THE PRECISION IT IS DEFENDING, not just its value.

Measured on main 855b754 after I proposed tightening NormTolerance and was wrong:

  float32 machine epsilon   1.1920929e-07
  NormTolerance             1e-06          8.4x headroom
  Dtype.Float32 is real     codec/sidecar.scala:953, :978, :1068

A unit vector stored as float32 and widened back to double does not return with norm 1.0. So
1e-6 is an ordinary margin for a float32 round trip, not the indefensible slack I claimed. I
computed the justification against float64 normalization error (~1e-15), concluded the
constant was absurd, and told another agent to file a bead for tightening it. I checked the
arithmetic of my claim and never checked its premise.

WHY THIS IS A REAL DEFECT AND NOT JUST MY MISTAKE: nothing in production exercises the slack --
every L2 construction in main either divides by the norm first (vector.scala:40) or goes
through l2() (baselines.scala:234, :302, grakern distance.scala:253). A constant that protects
a path no current caller takes, and states nothing about what it protects, invites exactly the
reasoning I did. The next reader computes against whatever precision they have in mind and
proposes a change that would break float32 providers the moment we acquire one.

SCOPE: document, do not change any value.

  embed-core vector.scala:57   NormTolerance 1e-6   float32 round trip -- state it
  align hsmm.scala:202         Tolerance 1e-9       row-normalization/logsumexp float64
  align signature.scala:208, :332  Tolerance 1e-9   dimensionless ratio comparison
  interview Resolution.scala:74    Tolerance 1e-9   partition-of-unity sum, float64
  embed-grakern distance.scala:416 Epsilon 1e-9     distance indistinguishable from zero

Each states the precision or phenomenon it defends. Where the author does not KNOW, say so --
"unverified, chosen to match the align tolerance" is honest and is better than silence,
because it tells the next person the constant is inherited rather than derived.

AGENTS.md rule 7 already requires an empty-guard constant to declare its class. This is the
same rule for tolerances, and I am the measured instance of what happens without it.

P3. Comment-only. Occurs unmeasured for the float32 path itself: I have shown float32 storage
EXISTS and that 1e-6 is the right order for it; I have NOT traced a decoded float32 sidecar row
into ValidatedVector.of with Normalization.L2. Permits, not occurs. Whoever documents it should
either trace that or write that it is untraced.
set.title: tolerance constants state a value but not the precision they defend
